site.name: NIP
site.tagline: An in-kernel protocol stack for Named Data Networking
site.description: NIP is a research site around iStack, documenting the design, implementation and evaluation of bringing Named Data Networking (NDN) into the OS kernel.

home.title: Bringing Named Data Networking into the OS kernel
home.intro: NDN forwards by name rather than address and keeps per-packet state in the data plane. iStack takes NDN into the OS kernel for the first time while staying compatible with the existing address-based stack and socket interfaces.
home.paperTitle: iStack: A General and Stateful Name-based Protocol Stack for Named Data Networking
home.paperAuthors: Tianlong Li · Tian Song · Yating Yang
home.paperCaption: iStack · NSDI '24 · Beijing Institute of Technology
home.abstractShort: A kernel stack that brings NDN name resolution, per-packet state and address interfaces together without changing how applications use the network.
home.paperAbstract: iStack is the first NDN protocol stack implemented inside the OS kernel. It combines in-kernel name resolution, a two-layer face system and socket-compatible interfaces, keeping per-packet state and name-based forwarding on the kernel data path while preserving the existing network stack model.
home.statsNote: Values are reported in the NSDI '24 paper abstract. See the paper for the testbed, hardware and comparison methodology.
home.pillarsTitle: Four things the kernel had to relearn
home.pillarsIntro: Putting NDN into a general-purpose OS is not a matter of moving a userspace forwarder into the kernel; it is a matter of repositioning names, state and address interfaces.
home.pillarKernelDesc: Forwarding and local delivery share one name resolution architecture, keeping lookups on the kernel data path.
home.pillarFacesDesc: A face abstraction over MAC, IP and port lets name semantics sit on top of the existing kernel network architecture.
home.pillarSocketDesc: Applications keep their socket programming model while NDN capabilities are introduced incrementally.
home.pillarEvidenceDesc: 6.50 Gbps throughput, a 16.25× speedup and 46.08% lower cached-packet latency form the paper's core evidence.
home.architectureIntro: iStack puts name resolution, per-packet state and address abstraction into one kernel stack. Interest and Data travel the same path, carrying different state.
home.principleNameTitle: Resolve the name, then choose a direction
home.principleNameDesc: One name resolution architecture serves both network-layer forwarding and local packet demultiplexing.
home.principleFacesTitle: Let address interfaces speak in names
home.principleFacesDesc: The two-layer face system folds MAC, IP and port into one abstraction without asking devices to understand NDN.
home.principleStateTitle: Keep state on the data path
home.principleStateDesc: PIT, CS and FIB form the core of per-packet state; compact data structures keep the memory cost in check.
home.stateNote: The PIT tracks pending Interests, the CS caches Data, and the FIB maps name prefixes to faces.
home.faceNote: MAC, IP and port remain the reality of devices and links; faces bring them under name semantics.
home.evidenceIntro: iStack set out to show not only that NDN can run in the kernel, but that it can run at usable performance. These results come from the NSDI '24 paper.
home.evidenceNote: Values are reported in the paper abstract. Testbed setup, hardware and comparison details are in the paper itself.
home.notesIntro: Design trade-offs, implementation details and experimental observations appear as notes before they settle into documentation.
home.finalTitle: Read the stack. Then put it to work.
home.finalIntro: Start with the project overview, or open the NSDI '24 paper and PDF directly.
